title: New gear this week: 8 releases from a Flytanium EDC knife to a meteorite-dial GMT
byline: AN About the author Allie Nguyen More by Allie Nguyen →
excerpt: Eight fresh releases worth a look this Saturday, from Flytanium's $49.95 Pork Chop folder and Roxon's modular Flex Go multitool to a meteorite-dial Jack Mason GMT and Kuoe's 80-hour Royal Smith.
content:

Saturday is a good day to catch up on what actually launched this week. Eight new releases stood out from the pile, and the spread runs wide: two knives, a modular multitool, two very different watches, a travel charger with a retractable cable, a walnut headphone stand and a stackable cup from Yeti.

Every price below was checked against the maker’s own store or a verified listing today, and each pick links straight to its buy route. A few bigger stories from our own week get their own links at the bottom.

The short list

  • Flytanium Pork Chop, $49.95: a 2.4-inch sheepsfoot EDC folder with a crossbar lock
  • Roxon Flex Go, $69.99: a multitool that lets you swap its tool loadout
  • GiantMouse Butcher Knife, $215: a full-tang Nitro B blade built for brisket duty
  • Jack Mason Strat-o-timer GMT Triton Meteorite, $1,449: a flyer GMT with a real meteorite dial
  • Kuoe Royal Smith 90-006, $990: a Roman numeral dress watch with an 80-hour reserve
  • Twelve South CableSnap 65W, $49.99: a travel charger with a retractable USB-C cable
  • Audioengine Headphone Stand, $59: walnut, and the first stand the speaker brand has made
  • YETI Rambler 16 oz Stackable Cup, $33: the pint-size Rambler that nests for storage

Flytanium Pork Chop, $49.95

Small sheepsfoot blades cut bigger than they look, and the Pork Chop leans all the way into that idea. Its 2.4-inch modified sheepsfoot blade is ground from 14C28N stainless, a steel that sharpens easily and shrugs off rust, and it rides in contoured G-10 scales over nested steel liners.

The ambidextrous crossbar lock means the knife opens and closes the same way with either hand. Flytanium cuts the closed package to 5.8 inches overall and 3.1 ounces, with a reversible deep-carry clip. Five colors are live at $49.95, and a harder S90V blade upgrade runs $69.95.

Price: $49.95
Where to buy: Amazon

Roxon Flex Go, $69.99

Most multitools lock you into the loadout the factory picked. Flex Go treats its tools like cartridges instead: eight slots accept swappable frames from Roxon’s Flex system, with more than 40 add-on tools in the catalog, so the pliers ride next to the implements you actually use.

A pre-installed build at $69.99 packs needle-nose and regular pliers, wire cutters, a DIN 1.4116 blade, scissors, an awl, openers, a diamond file and a double-ended bit driver, plus a toothpick and tweezers. It closes to 3.46 inches at 6.12 ounces. A bare frame-only version sells for $48.

Price: $69.99
Where to buy: Roxon

GiantMouse Butcher Knife, $215

GiantMouse built its name on folding knives designed with Jens Ansø and Jesper Voxnaes, and its kitchen line carries the same thinking to the cutting board. The Butcher runs a 9.33-inch Nitro B blade with a deep belly for long slicing strokes through brisket and primal cuts.

Construction is full tang with a satin finish, and the green canvas Micarta handle fills the hand without hot spots. Overall length is 14.08 inches at 8 ounces, the edge leaves Maniago, Italy at 17 degrees, and care is hand wash only. A red G10 handle version runs $225.

Price: $215
Where to buy: GiantMouse

Jack Mason Strat-o-timer GMT Triton Meteorite, $1,449

A sliver of the Muonionalusta meteorite forms the dial on this Triton, cut and tinted icy blue, so no two watches in the run share the same pattern. Under it sits Miyota’s 9075, a true flyer GMT with a jumping hour hand, regulated in house to plus or minus five seconds a day.

Case dimensions run 40mm across and 13.2mm thick, with a 48-click ceramic bezel in Pepsi colors, sapphire crystals front and back, and 200 meters of water resistance. Super-LumiNova BGW9 handles the dark. Jack Mason assembles and regulates each watch in the USA, and pre-orders at $1,449 start shipping the week of November 16.

Price: $1,449
Where to buy: Jack Mason

Kuoe Royal Smith 90-006, $990

Kyoto’s Kuoe put Roman numerals on a dial for the first time with the Royal Smith 90-006, and it built the watch around Miyota’s new Caliber 9085. The automatic movement runs about 80 hours on a wind, wears Geneva stripes across its rotor, and drives plume hands with a heat-blued seconds hand.

A two-layer dial comes in Ivory, Blue and Green, in 35mm and 39mm cases on Italian leather straps. Kuoe sells the watch only through its own store at $990, and pre-orders are estimated to ship from February 2027. An 80-hour reserve in a dress watch under four figures is the part that got my attention.

Price: $990
Where to buy: Kuoe

Twelve South CableSnap 65W, $49.99

Travel chargers usually mean a brick plus a cable you forgot to pack. CableSnap builds the cable in: a flat USB-C lead pulls out to 29 inches on a spring-loaded reel and retracts when you’re done, and the body still finds room for extra USB-C and USB-A ports.

Output runs to 65W shared across whatever is plugged in, with the USB-A port topping out at 18W, so a laptop, a tablet and a phone can share one outlet. UK Type G and EU Type C adapters ride along in the box, the US plug folds flat, and colors are Dune, Coastal and Slate.

Price: $49.99
Where to buy: Amazon

Audioengine Headphone Stand, $59

Audioengine has made desktop speakers for two decades, and the Headphone Stand is its first move into holding the other half of a desk setup. It’s real wood with a walnut finish matched to the company’s speaker cabinets, shaped as a hollow rectangle with rounded edges.

An open form keeps a set of over-ears visible instead of buried in a drawer, and the footprint suits the corner of a desk next to a pair of A2+ or HD6 speakers. At $59 it’s priced like the accessory it is, and it’s in stock now at Audioengine.

Price: $59
Where to buy: Audioengine

YETI Rambler 16 oz Stackable Cup, $33

Yeti’s 16 oz Rambler cup takes the usual recipe, 18/8 stainless steel with double-wall vacuum insulation, and shapes it to stack. A tapered base still fits standard cupholders, and the shoulder lets one cup nest into the next, so a set of four stores in the space of about two.

A color-matched MagSlider lid comes standard. Yeti is clear that the magnetic slider is splash resistant rather than leakproof, so this is a desk and camp cup, not a gym-bag bottle. It’s dishwasher safe, weighs 0.48 pounds and carries a five-year warranty at $33 a cup.

Price: $33
Where to buy: YETI

Already on Gadgeteer this week

Sony rebuilt the 1979 Walkman headphone as the MDR-3R with USB-C, and it picked up two pieces from us this week, a $59.99 revival story and a Walkman-look follow-up. Piaget’s Andy Warhol Camouflage builds Warhol’s self-portrait from 27 pieces of stone and gold at $90,600, and it got its own feature.

Tivoli’s Model One BT Naturals radio landed this week too, and Victorinox numbered its Huntsman Year of the Goat at 8,888 pieces for $99. This morning brought the Timex Atelier Marine M1a in blue at $950, and Allie’s Crocs Peanuts Joe Cool Classic Lined Clog piece is up today too.

That’s the week in new gear. The Pork Chop and the Flex Go are the easy buys at this money, the Triton is the one I’d stop scrolling for, and the CableSnap is the charger most travel bags have been missing. We’ll do it again next Saturday.
